root_cause.text: After the first L2 VMRUN, KVM incorrectly uses the current L2 RIP from vmcb12 as NextRIP in vmcb02 during save/restore operations, even though NextRIP has already been updated by the CPU and/or KVM, causing incorrect instruction pointer values for nested guests with NRIPS disabled.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the logic from unconditionally using `vmcb12_rip` when NRIPS is not exposed to L1, to only using it when `svm->nested.nested_run_pending` is true (i.e., on the first nested run). The commit message explicitly states: "after L2 runs the first time, NextRIP will be updated by the CPU and/or KVM, and the current RIP is no longer the correct value to use in vmcb02. Hence, after save/restore, use the current RIP if and only if a nested run is pending, otherwise use NextRIP." The fix adds the condition `!svm->nested.nested_run_pending` to both the main NextRIP assignment and the `soft_int_next_rip` assignment, ensuring that after the first VMRUN, the already-updated NextRIP is used instead of the stale RIP value from vmcb12.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix NextRIP initialization to only use vmcb12 RIP on first L2 run, not during save/restore, by adding nested_run_pending check to prevent incorrect RIP injection.
intent_record.what: Restructured the NextRIP initialization logic by inverting the outer condition from checking guest_cpu_cap_has(NRIPS) to checking boot_cpu_has(NRIPS), and added a nested condition checking !svm->nested.nested_run_pending. Updated comments to clarify that NextRIP stuffing only applies on first L2 run, not during save/restore. Applied the same condition change to soft interrupt NextRIP initialization.
intent_record.how: The change fixes a bug where NextRIP was incorrectly being set from vmcb12 during save/restore operations (when nested_run_pending is false) even when the guest doesn't support NRIPS. Now, the L2 RIP from vmcb12 is only used on the first L2 run after VMRUN; on subsequent runs (save/restore), the CPU/KVM-updated NextRIP value is preserved. This prevents incorrect RIP values from being injected during event delivery after VM state restoration.

grouping_result.intent: Fix NextRIP initialization to only use vmcb12 RIP on first L2 run, not during save/restore, by adding nested_run_pending check to prevent incorrect RIP injection.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by adding a nested_run_pending check to prevent using vmcb12 RIP as NextRIP during save/restore operations after the first L2 VMRUN. This fix ensures NextRIP is only initialized from vmcb12 on the initial L2 run, not on subsequent operations where the CPU/KVM has already updated NextRIP, which is exactly what the vulnerability describes.

candidates.rationale: This line unconditionally sets next_rip to vmcb12_rip (the current L2 RIP from vmcb12) whenever NRIPS is not exposed to L1 but supported in hardware. During save/restore operations after the first L2 VMRUN, this causes incorrect RIP injection because it overwrites the CPU-updated NextRIP with the stale vmcb12 RIP value, rather than only using vmcb12_rip on the first L2 run when nested_run_pending is true.

This line unconditionally copies next_rip from vmcb12 (via svm->nested.ctl.next_rip) when NRIPS is exposed to L1. During save/restore after the first L2 VMRUN, this overwrites the CPU-updated NextRIP with the stale vmcb12 value, causing incorrect instruction pointer values for nested guests. The fix requires checking nested_run_pending to only apply this on the first L2 run.

During save/restore operations after the first L2 VMRUN, this overwrites the CPU-updated NextRIP with the stale vmcb12 RIP value, causing incorrect instruction pointer injection for nested guests. The vulnerability occurs because this assignment lacks a nested_run_pending check to restrict it to only the first L2 run.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit INTRODUCES the fix for the vulnerability. The vulnerability root cause states that KVM incorrectly uses the current L2 RIP from vmcb12 as NextRIP in vmcb02 even though NextRIP has already been updated. The commit fixes this by: (1) Adding `to->next_rip = from->next_rip;` to sync the next_rip field from vmcb12 to vmcb02 in __nested_copy_vmcb_control_to_cache() at line 374, (2) Modifying nested_vmcb02_prepare_control() to accept vmcb12_rip parameter and implementing proper logic: if nrips_enabled, use next_rip from vmcb12 (line 676); otherwise if hardware supports NRIPS, stuff vmcb02's next_rip with the actual L2 RIP (line 678). This correctly handles both cases - when NRIPS is exposed to L1 and when it's not. The function calls are updated to pass vmcb12->save.rip (line 763) and svm->vmcb->save.rip (line 1621) respectively. The code shows the vulnerable construct is being FIXED, not introduced.

The root cause describes that KVM incorrectly uses the current L2 RIP from vmcb12 as NextRIP in vmcb02 even though NextRIP has already been updated. The commit adds proper handling by: (1) syncing next_rip field from vmcb12 to vmcb02 in __nested_copy_vmcb_control_to_cache (line +to->next_rip = from->next_rip), (2) adding logic in nested_vmcb02_prepare_control to conditionally set next_rip based on whether nrips is exposed to L1 (lines +if (svm->nrips_enabled) vmcb02->control.next_rip = svm->nested.ctl.next_rip; else if (boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_NRIPS)) vmcb02->control.next_rip = vmcb12_rip), and (3) passing vmcb12_rip as a parameter to nested_vmcb02_prepare_control. This is a fix-introducing commit, not a bug-introducing commit. The vulnerable construct (incorrect use of L2 RIP) is being corrected here.
